findings.issue: The fan-out sizing advice names the parent `--max-iterations` flag, but a fan-out lineage's iteration cap is its own `iterations` value: `fanout-run.cjs` writes `lineage.iterations` into the lineage prompt as `config.maxIterations` (line 1720) and onto the lineage CLI as `--max-iterations=` (line 1820), defaulting to 12 when unset (line 1808). The `--max-iterations` bound on the `/deep:review` call only sets the parent `config.maxIterations` (the per-executor `--iters` value fills the lineage entry), and the parent never runs loop iterations on a fan-out run, so sizing that flag does not fund the depth-1 band the sentence is about.

fix.old: Size `--max-iterations` so half of it covers `ceil(nodes / lineages) * dimensions`.
fix.new: Size each lineage's iteration cap (the `--iters=N` value on its `--executor`/`--executors` entry, which `fanout-run.cjs` passes as that lineage's `--max-iterations`, 12 when unset) so half of it covers `ceil(nodes / lineages) * dimensions`.

findings.issue: The doc says the extension step prints a warning when a re-stop is likely. The step computes that warning only when `config.antiConvergence.stopPolicy === "convergence"` (deep-review.yaml:576), while the shipped config template sets `antiConvergence.stopPolicy` to `fail-closed` (deep-review-config.json:15) and `step_create_config` populates only the top-level `stopPolicy` (deep-review.yaml:882-ish `stopPolicy: "{stop_policy}"`), which is the key the stop decision actually reads (convergence.cjs:1396). Under the documented `stopPolicy: convergence` default the warning is therefore never printed, so an operator who counts on it gets no signal that the extension will immediately re-stop on `all_dimensions_clean`.

The section presents the review dimensions as configured in `assets/review-mode-contract.yaml`, but two rows carry names that contract does not use: `Spec-Alignment / Traceability` (line 151) and `Completeness / Maintainability` (line 152), where the contract's ids and labels are `traceability` and `maintainability` (review-mode-contract.yaml:75-82). The names matter because the workflow treats any configured name outside the four canonical ids as a custom dimension (deep-review.yaml:826), so binding `spec-alignment` or `completeness` silently produces custom dimensions instead of the canonical ones. The section also omits the contract's `customDimensionRule` (review-mode-contract.yaml:88), which orders a custom name after the canonical four, and never says a custom name is accepted at all.
